Claire —

Thanks for sending this over. Quick summary up front (so you can paste into the questionnaire):
- Persisted data: request metadata and minimal routing headers are stored for 30 days by default; complete request/response payloads are stored for 14 days for debugging/quality analysis and then deleted unless the customer opts into longer retention.
- Backups/snapshots: nightly backups of control plane configs only (retained 90 days). We do NOT include customer request/response payloads in distributed point-in-time backups for hosted tenants.
- Erasure SLA: standard hosted API erasure requests are processed within 72 hours; purges from all short-term caches and immediate deletion from active storage occur as part of that workflow, with full propagation and verification within 30 days.

I'll paste the more detailed technical responses below for your security team to copy into the spreadsheet. Marissa / Dev — tagging you for the tech detail and evidence pack.

— Evelyn

--- Detailed responses (for the questionnaire) ---
Q1: Which data elements are persisted?
A1: For hosted API customers the following are persisted by default: request metadata (timestamp, route, model id, request/response token counts), routing headers required for multi-tenant isolation (tenant id, region hint), and short-term request/response payload snapshots for troubleshooting. By default payload snapshots are retained 14 days and then removed. Customers may opt into longer retention (30/90/365d) under contract; retention extensions are stored in the tenant policy and logged.

Q1a: Are user-generated inputs or model outputs stored long term?
A1a: Not by default. Long-term storage of complete inputs/outputs only occurs when a customer explicitly enables archival retention through the Console or during onboarding (and is reflected in the tenant's retention policy).

Q2: Backups and snapshots — what is included and where are they stored?
A2: We perform nightly backups of control-plane metadata (deployments, tenant policies, routing tables) with 90-day retention in encrypted object storage in the same region as the control plane. We do NOT include transient request/response payload snapshots in those backups for hosted tenants. In rare cases where a customer requests a managed export (for a regulatory need), we create an export package and deliver it over a pre-authorized, encrypted transfer link.

Q3: Customer-initiated erasure — process and timelines
A3: Erasure request flow:
- Customer submits erasure via Console or by emailing erase@redwood.com with tenant id and scope.
- Ticket created and triaged by Ops within 4 hours.
- Active storage deletion (hot and warm stores) initiated within 24–72 hours.
- Cache eviction (KV/prefix caches and streaming buffer) executed immediately during deletion operation.
- Background propagation (index/analytics de-duplication) completes within 30 days.
- Final verification evidence (audit log of deletion steps) shared as a signed PDF on request.

Q4: Geographical residency and controls
A4: Hosted API tenancy is region-aware; data that we persist is kept in the region selected at tenant onboarding. We support region pinning (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1). Cross-region replication for persisted data does not occur unless explicitly enabled via an enterprise agreement.

Q5: Backups and disaster recovery for persisted data
A5: For hosted customers, the only backed-up items are control-plane configuration artifacts. In the event of a platform outage we provide failover options via warm standby clusters; customer payload snapshots are not part of DR backups unless the customer has an explicit archive subscription.

Q6: Evidence and attestations
A6: We can provide SOC 2 Type II report excerpts, audit logs for retention policy changes, and a redacted evidence pack demonstrating deletion runs for a test tenant. See attached evidence pack and diagram.

Hi Jake / Claire —

Responding with clarifications from the infra and compliance teams:

1) Encryption and keying
- All persisted data (including payload snapshots) are encrypted at rest using AES-256. For hosted API customers we use tenant-scoped envelope keys managed in our KMS; the envelope keys themselves are rotated quarterly. For customers requiring dedicated key management we offer a BYOK/HSM integration as part of an enterprise plan.

2) Analytics, indexes, and post-purge visibility
- Aggregation pipelines used for metrics (token counts, latency percentiles) only store aggregated numeric metrics and do not retain verbatim customer inputs/outputs. Indexes that support routing or search are maintained on control-plane metadata and do not contain payload content. Where we generate redacted logs for debugging, redaction occurs prior to any downstream indexing. After a deletion/purge operation we run a verification job that scans index backends and analytics buckets for remnants; that verification result is included in the deletion verification PDF.

3) Sample verification and evidence
- I've attached a redacted sample verification (evidence-pack-redacted.zip) and the retention-and-purge-workflow.pdf. The verification PDF contains timestamps for each step, operator IDs (redacted), and job ids. We can provide additional fields (full operator audit trail) under an NDA.

4) Timelines recap
- Default payload retention: 14 days (customer can request longer)
- Control-plane backups: nightly, 90-day retention
- Erasure initial processing: 24–72 hours; final verification complete within 30 days

If you'd like, Dev can join a 30-minute tech call to walk through the flow and provide the deletion verification example live.

Best,
Marissa Cole
